scopeDeviation: ConnectionBadge.tsx was not in the original task's scope.allow list. It was touched because running the actual release gate surfaced a second real bug from the same root cause (the multiplayer e2e spec's assertions against the connection-status region) that the task's stated acceptance criteria could not be met without fixing. Flagging the deviation rather than silently expanding scope.
implementation: Four distinct, separately-diagnosed problems surfaced by actually running tools/validate.ps1 and tools/package.ps1 end to end, not by inspection: (1) ActionPanel's 'Reset' button and CameraControls's 'Reset view' button both matched Playwright's substring-based getByRole name locator - gave ActionPanel's button an explicit aria-label="Reset encounter" plus a visible <span aria-hidden> label, which in turn broke ActionPanel.test.tsx's own exact-match Vitest/RTL queries (RTL defaults to exact name matching, Playwright defaults to substring) - updated those queries and both e2e spec files to the new name. (2) ConnectionBadge's adjacent aria-hidden and sr-only <span> siblings concatenate with no separator in raw textContent (though the accessible name itself is unaffected, since it comes from an explicit aria-label on the container) - Playwright's toContainText reads raw textContent, so 'Live' + 'Live sync connected' rendered as 'LiveLive sync connected' and failed a not-toContainText assertion - fixed with a leading space in the sr-only span. (3) PowerShell's $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop' does not catch non-zero exit codes from native processes (npm/dotnet/python) - validate.ps1 and package.ps1 were both rewritten to check $LASTEXITCODE after every native invocation via an explicit Invoke-Checked helper (validate.ps1) / inline checks (package.ps1), so a real e2e failure now actually stops the pipeline instead of silently producing a submission zip anyway. (4) After fixing (1)-(3), a genuinely new failure appeared in multiplayer.spec.ts: 'Test timeout of 100000ms exceeded' with no specific failing assertion. Root-caused by summing the test's own deliberate waits - 12s quiet-connection check + 25s offline-detection wait + 30s reconnect wait = 67s of waiting that is load-bearing (it verifies real SignalR timing thresholds documented in combatHub.ts) - against the suite's 100s default timeout, leaving too little headroom for page/model load and the remaining interaction steps. Fixed by raising this single test's budget via test.setTimeout(150_000) rather than shortening any wait, since shortening would break what the test is actually verifying.
